text.p: Furniture retailer Rhodes Inc said on Tuesday it would merge with Heilig-Meyers Co, a home furnishings chain, in a stock swap.
The company said in a statement that, following the merger, Rhodes will be a subsidiary of Heilig-Meyers. The definitive agreement was unanimously approved by Rhodes' board of directors.

The accord entitles Rhodes shareholders to receive one Heilig-Meyers common share for every two shares of Rhodes common stock, or an total of about 4.6 million shares of Heilig-Meyers stock for all outstanding Rhodes shares.
Heilig-Meyers common shares closed on Tuesday at 14-1/4, down 5/8. Rhodes common shares closed at 10-5/8, up 1-1/2.

The merger is subject to Hart-Scott-Rodino anti-trust clearance, approval by Rhodes shareholders and other conditions. The transaction is structured as a tax-free exchange of shares. The merged companies on a combined basis had sales of about $1.5 billion and 824 stores for fiscal year ended February 29, 1996.
